investigation.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed between 09:07 and 09:14 UTC on 2026-07-01 with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the 6-node production cluster had only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, both of which were already at capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the eval runner never received a VM ID or a remote state value, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigation.rootCause: The production Kubernetes cluster has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. Every new remote-agent pod request is rejected as Unschedulable before a VM is provisioned, so the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never completes, no evidence is written, and the vmIdPresent and remoteState assertions cannot be evaluated. This is a resource-capacity constraint in the production infrastructure, not an eval configuration or code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to this observability eval at this time.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: existing remote-agent pods or other workloads have consumed all available VM slots on the only two nodes that carry this extended resource, leaving no capacity for new probe pods.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not match the pod's required node affinity/selector, meaning the schedulable pool for remote-agent pods is structurally limited to 2 nodes regardless of overall cluster size.

Tertiary — leaked or zombie remote-agent pods from prior eval runs holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if cleanup (withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs line 1883) failed in a previous run, stale pods may be occupying the resource.
Lower confidence — cluster scaling not triggered: the cluster autoscaler either is not configured for kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes or did not provision a new node in time for the eval window.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed between 09:07 and 09:14 UTC on 2026-07-01 with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the 6-node production cluster had only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, both of which were already at capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the eval runner never received a VM ID or a remote state value, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigations.rootCause: The production Kubernetes cluster has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. Every new remote-agent pod request is rejected as Unschedulable before a VM is provisioned, so the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never completes, no evidence is written, and the vmIdPresent and remoteState assertions cannot be evaluated. This is a resource-capacity constraint in the production infrastructure, not an eval configuration or code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to this observability eval at this time.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: existing remote-agent pods or other workloads have consumed all available VM slots on the only two nodes that carry this extended resource, leaving no capacity for new probe pods.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in sequence between 09:09 and 09:14 UTC on 2026-07-01 with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: the production cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule a new kata.peerpods.io/vm pod because 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resource capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1918) never completed, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was returned, causing a total contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in check-expectations.json lines 266–270.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 nodes that carry that resource type. Simultaneously, 4 other nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. The combined effect is that no node in the 6-node cluster can accept a new remote-agent pod, causing every eval attempt to time out in the Unschedulable state (~138–147 s) before the eval runner's timeout fires. This is an infrastructure capacity or configuration constraint, not an application code defect. No evidence of a user-traffic or production incident signal is present; the impact is localized to the AURA observability eval suite for the remote-agents feature in the production-api runtime environment.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: existing remote-agent pods (from prior eval runs, user workloads, or leaked pods from failed cleanup) are consuming all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new scheduling attempts. Preemption was attempted and found no victims, confirming slots are held by non-preemptable workloads.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector, reducing the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes. If the affinity rules were recently tightened or node labels changed, the effective capacity could have dropped to zero even with previously sufficient VM slot counts.

TERTIARY — Pod cleanup failure from a prior eval run: the eval runner uses withCleanup (run-status-probes.mjs line 1916) to track and remove created resources; if a prior run's cleanup did not complete (e.g., due to a runner crash or timeout), orphaned pods may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and blocking new scheduling.

LOWER CONFIDENCE — Cluster node count reduction: if the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes were recently cordoned, drained, or removed from the pool, the total allocatable VM capacity would have dropped, but no node-change evidence is present in the packet.
